title: Hibernate-and-wake round-trip preserves storage and re-emits doWakeUp exactly once
asA: developer whose HubObject hibernates when idle and wakes on the next message
iWant: the wake handler to run from cold and read the same lastBroadcast key from storage the pre-hibernate state persisted
soThat: a re-emerging client can catch up on the missed broadcast without a full re-sync

acceptanceCriteria.description: A HubObject that has processed a broadcast, hibernated (doHibernate emitted), and then woken (doWakeUp emitted once) resolves wake() with {lastBroadcast} equal to the serialised outbound payload the pre-hibernate broadcast persisted. A second wake() call resolves with {alreadyAwake: true, lastBroadcast: <same>} and does NOT emit a second doWakeUp. The wake handler is idempotent-by-contract per ADR-3405.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a HubObject with one persisted lastBroadcast that has hibernated
acceptanceCriteria.when: wake() is called once, then again
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first wake emits doWakeUp once and returns lastBroadcast; the second wake reports alreadyAwake without a second event

acceptanceCriteria.description: F-5 cold-start reconstruction: after a broadcast has been processed and hibernate has fired, a fresh HubObject INSTANCE constructed against the same storage (simulating Cloudflare's wake-on-message: the pre-hibernate instance is discarded and a new one is minted from cold), when wake() is called, reads lastBroadcast from storage and returns {lastBroadcast: <same serialised payload>}; doWakeUp fires exactly once on the fresh instance's sink. The reconstruction happens over the same durable storage, not over transferred in-memory state.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh HubObject instance constructed against a storage that carries a persisted lastBroadcast
acceptanceCriteria.when: wake() is called on the fresh instance
acceptanceCriteria.then: wake returns lastBroadcast equal to the persisted value; doWakeUp emits once

acceptanceCriteria.description: F-5 wake-on-message: a hibernated HubObject that receives a webSocketMessage during the hibernation window queues the message, wakes (doWakeUp emits once), reads the same storage, processes the queued message (e.g. a broadcast) and delivers to any connected sockets. The message is not dropped; the wake handler runs to completion before the message handler.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a hibernated HubObject with the message arriving from a re-emerging client
acceptanceCriteria.when: the driver delivers the webSocketMessage to the hibernated instance
acceptanceCriteria.then: wake fires, storage is read, and the message is processed after wake completes

acceptanceCriteria.description: Hibernate-before-broadcast: a HubObject that has hibernated without ever processing a broadcast persists no lastBroadcast key. wake() on the reconstructed instance returns {lastBroadcast: null} (not undefined; the field is present) and doWakeUp still emits exactly once.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a HubObject that hibernated without any broadcast
acceptanceCriteria.when: wake() is called on the reconstructed instance
acceptanceCriteria.then: wake returns lastBroadcast:null with the field present; doWakeUp emits once

acceptanceCriteria.description: Repeated hibernate-and-wake cycles: two hibernate + wake cycles on the same instance produce exactly two doHibernate and two doWakeUp records on the sink, alternating in strict order (hibernate1, wake1, hibernate2, wake2). No cycle produces duplicate records; the idempotent-by-contract guarantee (ADR-3405) holds per cycle.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a HubObject driven through two hibernate + wake cycles
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sink is inspected after the second wake
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sink records exactly two doHibernate and two doWakeUp in strict order
